headline: Dengue toll crosses 400 deaths as 6 more die in 24 hours
summary: Over 1,800 patients were hospitalized in a single day as the mosquito-borne disease continues to surge across Bangladesh.
details: Six more people have died of dengue in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll for this year to 415, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
A total of 1,886 new patients were admitted to hospitals nationwide within a single day, with the Dhaka Division recording the highest number of admissions at 755.
The recent fatalities were distributed across several regions: two deaths each in Dhaka and Chattogram divisions, and one each in Khulna and Rangpur divisions.
Other regional admissions include Barishal with 229, Chattogram with 272, Khulna with 264, Mymensingh with 89, Rajshahi with 188, and Sylhet with 29.
So far this year, 132,105 patients have been hospitalized for dengue, while 125,439 have been discharged after treatment.
The DGHS has been tracking dengue data since 2000, noting that the worst outbreak occurred in 2023 with 1,705 deaths and over 321,000 hospitalizations.
October alone has already seen 170 deaths, highlighting the continued severity of the current outbreak.

headline_marked: 3,430 workers to be [[recruited by Dhaka's two city corporations]]
headline: 3,430 workers to be recruited by Dhaka's two city corporations
summary: The new hires will be employed on a daily wage basis for waste removal, cleaning, and mosquito control activities.
details: The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) will recruit approximately 3,430 people on a daily wage basis. The DSCC will hire 2,026 workers, while the DNCC will hire 1,404.
The Ministry of Local Government approved the proposal on October 12. The recruits will be primarily responsible for waste removal, cleaning, and cleaning activities, and mosquito control operations.

The Ministry has issued a strict warning to both city corporations to ensure no irregularities in the recruitment process. The authorities have been told that any irregularities will be the sole responsibility of the the hiring authorities.
According to the Finance Division's policy, the daily wage for a worker in the Dhaka city area will be 800 BDT. This amounts to a monthly wage of approximately 24,000 BDT.
The Ministry of Finance has recently updated its 'Outsourcing Service Procurement Policy 2025', updated on September 21, which prohibits the hiring of workers through private firms for these roles.
The city corporations must hire workers directly or through the same approved specialized institution, the Infrastructure Investment Facilitation Company (IIFC).

The CEOs of both city corporations have stated that they are seeking to ensure a transparency and accountability in the recruitment process following the guidelines from the Local Government Ministry.
Experts suggest that the formation of a neutral committee to oversee the recruitment process to be avoid political influence, which has been a reported issue in previous recruitments.
